title: Split a vague verdict into its causes
statement: Split a vague complaint about generated media, such as 'soulless', into its separate causes, such as voice, gesture, reaction, pacing, framing and casting, because each has a different fix.
example: One review resolved a 'soulless' verdict on a generated guide character's delivery into five causes, each with its own fix, and then suggested casting as a sixth.
detail: First-round feedback on a Grade 9 prototype said its guide character's lines were mostly good but felt a little soulless (`g9/sources/Othello_1_Feedback_DevFactory.md`, line 173). The written response split that paragraph into four separate things fixed by different people, then resolved 'soulless' into flat vocal prosody (voice direction), absent or looped gesture (animation), no reaction (performance), uniform pacing (the edit) and unvarying framing (shot design), and its next section suggested casting as a sixth and likelier cause (lines 175, 179 and 190).
against: The breakdown is a review note, which the document says "is offered as rationale and has not been confirmed" (`g9/sources/Othello_1_Feedback_DevFactory.md`, line 13).

evidence.quote: they just feel a little bit soulless at the moment.
Four separate things, and they are fixed by different people: the script is mostly good; some lines read vague; the delivery feels soulless; and the face may not be needed throughout.

"Soulless" resolves into causes with different fixes: flat vocal prosody is voice direction, absent or looped gesture is animation, no reaction is performance, uniform pacing is the edit, and unvarying framing is shot design.
Section 4.2 suggests a sixth and likelier one.
The soullessness may be substantially a casting problem rather than a performance problem
